speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To help you with your acute diarrhea, please tell me how many times you have had loose stools in the last 24 hours and if you have experienced any fever or blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea (Clostridioides difficile infection). The patient recently took levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia and now presents with frequent watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping, which is highly suspicious for C. diff. I will request a C. difficile toxin assay and a stool culture to confirm the diagnosis.
